mcqs.question: Which statement correctly distinguishes evaporation from boiling?

options.A: Evaporation occurs only at the surface of a liquid at any temperature, while boiling occurs throughout the liquid when its vapor pressure equals atmospheric pressure.
options.B: Evaporation requires the liquid to reach its boiling point, while boiling can occur at any temperature.
options.C: Both evaporation and boiling occur only at the surface of the liquid.
options.D: Boiling is a surface phenomenon that causes cooling, whereas evaporation does not involve heat exchange.

mcqs.answer: Evaporation occurs only at the surface of a liquid at any temperature, while boiling occurs throughout the liquid when its vapor pressure equals atmospheric pressure.
mcqs.explanation: Evaporation is a surface phenomenon that can happen at any temperature; molecules with enough kinetic energy leave the surface. Boiling occurs when the liquid's vapor pressure equals the external pressure, producing bubbles throughout the bulk. Option A captures this difference. Options B, C, and D contain incorrect statements about the nature of the two processes.

mcqs.question: Which of the following changes will most increase the rate of evaporation of water placed in an open container?

options.A: Decreasing the temperature of the water
options.B: Increasing the atmospheric pressure above the water
options.C: Increasing the exposed surface area of the water
options.D: Reducing the wind speed over the water surface

mcqs.answer: Increasing the exposed surface area of the water
mcqs.explanation: A larger surface area allows more molecules to escape per unit time, raising the evaporation rate. Lower temperature (A) and higher pressure (B) reduce evaporation, while less wind (D) also slows it down. Hence option C is correct.

mcqs.learning_point: Understand the cooling effect of evaporation
mcqs.question: Why does the remaining liquid become cooler when evaporation occurs?

options.A: Energy is absorbed from the liquid to break intermolecular bonds, leaving the remaining molecules with lower average kinetic energy.
options.B: Evaporation releases latent heat to the surroundings, raising the temperature of the liquid.
options.C: Molecules with low kinetic energy escape first, reducing the average kinetic energy of the liquid.
options.D: Evaporation converts the liquid into a solid, which releases heat.

mcqs.answer: Energy is absorbed from the liquid to break intermolecular bonds, leaving the remaining molecules with lower average kinetic energy.
mcqs.explanation: During evaporation, high‑energy molecules leave the surface, and the energy required to overcome intermolecular forces is taken from the liquid, decreasing its average kinetic energy and thus its temperature. Option B is opposite to the actual effect, C incorrectly states low‑energy molecules escape, and D confuses evaporation with freezing.

mcqs.question: Which of the following is NOT an everyday application that relies on the principle of evaporation?

options.A: Sweating of the human body to cool down
options.B: Drying of wet clothes hung on a line
options.C: Operation of a household refrigerator using a compressor
options.D: Cooling of a pond surface on a hot sunny day

mcqs.answer: Operation of a household refrigerator using a compressor
mcqs.explanation: A refrigerator works on the principle of compression and condensation of a refrigerant, not on evaporation. Sweating, drying clothes, and pond surface cooling all involve water molecules escaping into air, which is evaporation. Therefore option C is the correct choice.
